claim: The extent to which genetic diversity can influence tree productivity through increased functional diversity is still unclear.

claim: The positive effect of tree functional diversity on community productivity was mainly due to an increase in functional diversity from species monocultures to mixtures.

claim: Herbivore leaf damage showed marginally significant negative overall effects on tree productivity.

claim: Herbivory represents the percentage of damaged area per leaf attacked by herbivores.

evidence: Definition of measurement

claim: The herbivory caused by chewers, gall formers, leaf miners, and rollers were collectively counted.
source: The herbivory caused by chewers, gall formers, leaf miners, and rollers were collectively counted.
evidence: Description of measurement

claim: Data from other plots of the BEF-China experiment were used to correct potential bias from only collecting damaged leaves.
source: Because we only collected damaged leaves in this study, we might have overestimated the herbivory per individual tree. We therefore used data from other plots of the BEF-China experiment (Schuldt et al., 2015), which did not exclude nondamaged leaves to correct the potential bias.
evidence: Description of correction method with citation to Schuldt et al., 2015

claim: Leaf damage of corresponding tree individuals from the former study was related to leaf damage excluding nondamaged leaves for all four species by linear regression (Pearson's correlation = 0.86–0.96, p < 0.001).
source: We related leaf damage of corresponding tree individuals from this former study (total leaf damage) to leaf damage excluding nondamaged leaves (damage per damaged leaf) for all four species by linear regression (Pearson's correlation = 0.86–0.96, p < 0.001) (Appendix 2—table 3).
evidence: Description of statistical analysis result

claim: Soil samples were taken on subplot level for the 1.1 and 1.4 diversity treatments, but on plot level for the 4.1 and 4.4 diversity treatments in 2017.
source: To be consistent with the species and genetic diversity treatment design, soil samples were taken on subplot level for the 1.1 and 1.4 diversity treatments, but, due to feasibility constraints, on plot level for the 4.1 and 4.4 diversity treatments in 2017.
evidence: Description of sampling method

claim: In each subplot or plot, five soil samples from the top 0–5 cm soil layer were collected from the four corners and the center of each subplot or plot and then mixed together.
source: In each subplot or plot, five soil samples from the top 0–5 cm soil layer were collected from the four corners and the center of each subplot or plot. The five samples were then mixed together.
evidence: Description of sampling method

claim: The nuclear rDNA internal transcribed spacer 2 (ITS2) region was amplified using primers ITS3F (GCATCGATGAAGAACGCAGC) and ITS4R (TCCTCCGCTTATTGATATGC).
source: We amplified the nuclear rDNA internal transcribed spacer 2 (ITS2) region using primers ITS3F (GCATCGATGAAGAACGCAGC) and ITS4R (TCCTCCGCTTATTGATATGC).
evidence: Description of molecular method

claim: The fungal OTU tables were rarefied to 10,975 reads to account for the different sequencing depths.
source: The fungal OTU tables were rarefied to 10,975 reads to account for the different sequencing depths.
evidence: Description of data processing method

claim: The sequences were assigned to taxonomic groups using the UNITE database.
source: We then assigned the sequences to taxonomic groups using the UNITE database (Nilsson et al., 2019).
evidence: Description of method with citation to Nilsson et al., 2019

claim: The Chao1 diversity index was used to quantify soil fungal diversity because most fungal species in the study were relatively rare and the Chao1 index can account well for rare species.
source: Based on the taxonomic and abundance information of every subplot or plot, the Chao1 diversity index (Chao, 1984) was used to quantify soil fungal diversity, because most fungal species in our study were relatively rare and the Chao1 index can account well for rare species (Chao, 1984).
evidence: Description of method with citations to Chao, 1984

claim: The basal area (BA) and the height (H) of all trees in the species × genetic diversity plots were measured in 2018.
source: We measured the basal area (BA) and the height (H) of all trees in the species × genetic diversity plots in 2018 (Bongers et al., 2020).
evidence: Description of measurements with citation to Bongers et al., 2020

claim: Individual tree biomass (kg) was calculated using the biomass equation (H × BA × CV) of the BEF-China experiment.
source: Individual tree biomass (kg) was calculated using the biomass equation (H × BA × CV) of the BEF-China experiment (Huang et al., 2018) in which CV is a correction factor for stem shape and wood density.
evidence: Description of calculation method with citation to Huang et al., 2018

claim: The biomass of individual trees was summed to subplot level to calculate tree community productivity (Mg ha–1).
source: We summed the biomass of individual trees to subplot level to calculate tree community productivity (Mg ha–1).
evidence: Description of calculation method

claim: Linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) were fitted with two types of contrast coding to determine how species and genetic diversity and their interaction affected tree functional diversity and trophic interactions.
source: To determine how species and genetic diversity and their interaction affected tree functional diversity and trophic interactions, linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) were fitted with two types of contrast coding.
evidence: Description of statistical method

claim: 'Plot' was used as a random variable in all LMMs since subplots were nested in plots.
source: For all LMMs, we used 'plot' as a random variable since subplots were nested in plots.
evidence: Description of statistical method

claim: The proportion of leaf damage caused by herbivores was angular transformed to meet the assumptions of linear mixed models.
source: To meet the assumptions of linear mixed models, the proportion of leaf damage caused by herbivores was angular transformed (Snedecor and Cochran, 1989).
evidence: Description of data transformation with citation to Snedecor and Cochran, 1989

claim: Structural equation models (SEMs) were fitted to assess causal hypotheses about how the effects of tree species and genetic diversity on community productivity could have been mediated via tree functional diversity and trophic interactions.
source: Second, we fitted SEMs and displayed the results in path-analysis diagrams (Grace, 2006) with the 'piecewiseSEM' package version 2.1.2 in R (Lefcheck, 2016) to assess causal hypotheses about how the effects of tree species and genetic diversity on community productivity could have been mediated via tree functional diversity and trophic interactions.
evidence: Description of statistical method with citations to Grace, 2006 and Lefcheck, 2016

claim: Noninformative pathways were sequentially dropped if their removal reduced the AICc of the SEMs by more than 2.
source: We sequentially dropped noninformative pathways if their removal reduced the AICc of the SEMs by more than 2 (Grace, 2006).

claim: Separate multigroup SEMs were fitted for species monocultures and mixtures since significant interactions between species and genetic diversity in the ANOVAs indicated that genetic diversity had different effects between species monocultures and the species mixtures.

claim: Tree species diversity increased tree productivity via increased tree functional diversity, reduced soil fungal diversity, and marginally reduced herbivory.
source: We found that tree species diversity increased tree productivity via increased tree functional diversity, reduced soil fungal diversity, and marginally reduced herbivory.

claim: The effects of tree genetic diversity on productivity via functional diversity and soil fungal diversity were negative in monocultures but positive in the mixture of the four tree species tested.
source: The effects of tree genetic diversity on productivity via functional diversity and soil fungal diversity were negative in monocultures but positive in the mixture of the four tree species tested.

claim: Both tree species and genetic diversity should be considered in afforestation given the complexity of interactions between species and genetic diversity, tree functional diversity and trophic feedbacks on productivity.
source: Given the complexity of interactions between species and genetic diversity, tree functional diversity and trophic feedbacks on productivity, we suggest that both tree species and genetic diversity should be considered in afforestation.

claim: Herbivory has negative effects on plant productivity via the reduction of leaf area.

evidence: Supported by citation to Zvereva et al., 2012

source: For example, it has been shown that in species-diverse grassland ecosystems, niche-complementarity between species can increase at the expense of reduced variation within species (van Moorsel et al., 2018; van Moorsel et al., 2019; Zuppinger-Dingley et al., 2014; Zvereva et al., 2012).

These may include unmeasured functional traits such as root traits (Bardgett et al., 2014) or unknown mechanisms underpinning effects of tree genetic diversity.

claim: The method of calculating functional diversity based on seed-family means has the advantage to be less circular.
